_comment: Records normalization config. Decisions (user 2026-10-09): log2(ops) is the primary frontier metric; core-year equivalents only for totals, as low/high ranges; totals over record-setting solves only; Bitcoin-puzzle compute reported separately. Factors are deliberately coarse. Target and slope values are sourced in analysis/normalization_sources.json (research 2026-10-09); method and rationale in analysis/normalization_method.md.

cpu_core_year_by_era._unit: 2020 core-year equivalents per CPU core-year, by year of the computation

device_year._fpga_note: FPGA throughput is very workload-specific; prefer iteration counts where available

lattice_model.native_unit: sieving dimension: frontier = solver-reported max sieving dimension of the record SVP-challenge solve (else d - d/ln d); targets = spec refined-primal sieving dimension beta'
lattice_model.slope_low_note: asymptotic BDGL classical sieving exponent (NIST core-SVP convention)
lattice_model.slope_high_note: Ducas-Stevens-van Woerden 2021 (EUROCRYPT), Fig. 7(b) triple_gpu fit 2^(0.367 n - 37.15) s, sieving dims 121-140; records' FLOP counts (their Table 1, max sieving dims 127-150) give 0.365. Our own fit over 2018-2026 records (0.18) was rejected as confounded by hardware/algorithm progress.
lattice_model.per_sieve_note: Gaps are per sieve call; the full primal attack adds roughly 2^9 for ML-KEM-512 (spec).
